Experimental-unit dimensions by two-dimensional marginal efficiency

Source: R/marginal_efficiency.R
marginal_efficiency_2d.Rd

Estimates the width and length of the experimental unit on the fitted coefficient-of-variation surface by a coordinate-wise marginal-efficiency criterion, as a closed-form alternative to the curvature criteria.

Usage

marginal_efficiency_2d(a, m, n, target_slope = 1)

Arguments

a, m, n

Positive parameters of the fitted coefficient-of-variation surface \(CV(x, y) = a\,x^{-m}\,y^{-n}\), with x the width and y the length in basic units.

target_slope

Positive target slope: the decrease in the coefficient of variation, in percentage points, per additional basic unit of the dimension considered. The same target is applied to width and length. Defaults to 1.

Value

A one-row data frame with columns criterion, width, length, area (all in basic units), cv (the predicted coefficient of variation at the solution) and K (the Gaussian curvature of the surface at that point).

Details

The marginal decreases of the surface are \(-\partial CV / \partial x = m\,CV / x\) and \(-\partial CV / \partial y = n\,CV / y\). Setting both equal to target_slope yields a unique positive solution with closed form \(x = (a\,m^{\,n+1} / (\tau\,n^{n}))^{1/(m+n+1)}\), \(y = (a\,n^{\,m+1} / (\tau\,m^{m}))^{1/(m+n+1)}\) and length-to-width ratio \(n/m\). This is a marginal criterion by coordinates, not a geometric-curvature criterion, and the result depends on the scale in which the coefficient of variation and the dimensions are expressed; the computation is in basic units and physical conversion is applied afterwards.

Examples

marginal_efficiency_2d(a = 22.95, m = 0.608, n = 0.232)
#>   criterion    width length     area       cv          K
#> 1  marginal 4.730084 1.8049 8.537331 7.779743 0.02394712
marginal_efficiency_2d(a = 22.95, m = 0.608, n = 0.232, target_slope = 0.5)
#>   criterion    width  length     area       cv          K
#> 1  marginal 6.894013 2.63061 18.13546 5.669419 0.01127319
